findings.title: Retry-count delete branch is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second `OR` branch of the `deleteMany` is just `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled: false`. `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table, so this SMS cron deletes any EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. As soon as the email or WhatsApp crons reuse this column for their own retry logic, their reminders will be silently removed by the SMS job. The branch should be scoped to `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: Falsy scheduleSMS result is counted as a failure, so reminders of SMS-locked accounts get deleted
findings.body: The new `else` branch increments `retryCount` whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value. In the Twilio provider, that function returns `undefined` on purpose when the user or team is locked for SMS sending (`smsLockState` LOCKED or REVIEW_NEEDED). That is a deliberate skip, not a delivery failure. Previously these reminders stayed in the table and could still be scheduled once an admin unlocked the account. Now they are permanently deleted after two cron runs, so a user under temporary review loses all upcoming SMS reminders. A deliberate skip should be told apart from a real scheduling error.

findings.title: DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron batch
findings.body: The `catch` block used to only log. It now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` first, which is not protected by its own try/catch. If that update fails (DB/connection error, or the row was deleted concurrently, which makes Prisma throw P2025), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler then returns a 500 and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped for this run. One bad reminder can stall SMS scheduling for everyone. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and swallow update errors.

findings.title: Transient errors are treated like permanent ones; two failures permanently drop the reminder
findings.body: Every exception in the try block increments `retryCount`, and after two increments the reminder is hard-deleted. That includes a Twilio outage or rate-limit response, and failures in unrelated code before sending such as `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl` or `customTemplate`. Two consecutive cron runs can be minutes apart, so a short provider outage now silently and permanently loses SMS reminders that would previously have been retried until the send date. The deletion is also not logged anywhere. Consider counting only non-retryable errors (e.g. invalid number) toward deletion, or allowing more attempts with logging.

findings.title: OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run
findings.body: Before this change, the `deleteMany` predicate (`method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now`) could use the `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index. Adding an `OR` branch on `retryCount`, which has no index and no `method` restriction, generally forces Postgres into a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table. That table includes all email and WhatsApp reminders and runs on every cron invocation. Scoping the second branch to `method = SMS` (or adding an index) would avoid this.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR adds logic that permanently deletes user reminders based on a failure counter, but no tests cover it. Cases worth covering: the increment on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result, the increment on a thrown error, deletion once `retryCount > 1`, and confirming that non-SMS reminders are untouched. Regressions here mean SMS reminders are silently lost.
